executive_assessment.text: Named health-risk locations and South Oropouche/Port of Spain corridor findings provide local differentiation, with qualitative plan and unvalidated susceptibility-model limits.

Municipal staffing, planning and funding constraints coexist with disaster-management units and community warning systems. Historical training and system descriptions do not establish response effectiveness.
South Oropouche launch plans and beneficiary/ecosystem targets are prospective; the registry does not verify current completion or measured resilience effects.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2023-11 reports: The health-risk assessment names Tunapuna-Piarco, Penal-Debe, Port of Spain and Tobago among localities especially vulnerable to flash-flood health impacts.
Source dated 2026-03-13 reports: Port of Spain, East-West Corridor, Valencia and low South Oropouche repeatedly rank high or very high.
Source dated not stated reports: Government reports a September 2023 launch of a US$10 million project for South Oropouche flood, sea-level and water-deficit resilience.
Source dated not stated reports: Project targets 9,758 direct beneficiaries and 175 hectares of coastal and wetland ecosystems.
Source dated not stated reports: Government cites flood vulnerability, population density and economic/cultural activity in selecting the basin; CAF says resident engagement is critical.

known_gaps.text: No Trinidad and Tobago country baseline was listed in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json.
The NAP's water-allocation conflict is the only explicit climate-FCV mechanism found; it concerns projected resource competition, not observed armed conflict or gang violence.
No inspected primary source documented crime, gangs or insecurity blocking local climate adaptation or service access; the reverse pathway remains an evidence gap.
The 2024 local-government article has qualitative case evidence and two Trinidad participant perspectives; its findings are not a representative municipal survey.
NAP service-access indicators have no underlying year stated in the cited passage; the 2026 model uses 2007 land cover and lacks independent quantitative validation.
The South Oropouche page reports launch-stage targets, not achieved reach or current project status; Ministry preparedness descriptions are self-reported and date to 2023 or earlier.

Full-text access gaps: 2019 government Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment PDF, IDB sea-level-rise study PDF and UNDP community-adaptation page could not be read; indexed excerpts were not used as findings.

Potential water-allocation conflict is a qualitative NAP risk. Named contamination-risk locations must not be turned into dispute hotspots; no full violence mechanism or reverse-FCV chain was verified.
The 2026 susceptibility model uses 2007 land cover and equal weights and lacks independent validation; its classes are not event probabilities or current exposure counts.
Municipal interviews are selective and ministry preparedness accounts are self-reported historical activities, not representative performance audits.
South Oropouche figures are launch-stage targets for a four-year project, not verified current delivery or achieved reach.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
